name: CR 26-051: DNR rewrite of non-landfill solid waste rules
what: DNR proposes revisions to chs. NR 157 and NR 500 to 526 governing non-landfill solid waste management; public comment open through Oct. 23, 2026.
pitch: Solid waste rules shape what county and municipal transfer stations, recycling operations and waste haulers must do — and touch DNR's cleanup and contamination oversight that WPR tracks.

name: CR 26-054: DATCP rules on storing flammable and hazardous liquids
what: DATCP proposes rules on storage of flammable, combustible and hazardous liquids, with a stated effect on small businesses; comment open through Nov. 6, 2026.
pitch: Tank and hazardous-liquid storage standards are the front end of the contamination cleanup cases WPR tracks, and they land on Marathon County farms, fuel dealers and small shops.

name: CR 26-049: DPI Tier I special education licensure dates and eligibility
what: DPI submitted a proposed rule changing Tier I special education licensure dates and which entities may request those licenses.
pitch: Special education staffing is a chronic squeeze for Wausau and rural Marathon County districts; who can request a Tier I license determines who can stand in front of students.
access: Proposed rule · submitted to Legislature, no comment deadline listed

name: CR 26-050: DPI special education program aide licenses
what: DPI submitted a proposed rule on special education program aide licenses.
pitch: Program aides are the backbone of special education classrooms; licensing changes affect hiring, pay and whether local districts can fill openings.
access: Proposed rule · submitted to Legislature, no comment deadline listed

name: CR 26-048: DPI intern licenses for teachers
what: DPI submitted a proposed rule on intern licenses.
pitch: Intern licenses are one pipeline districts use to staff hard-to-fill classrooms amid the teacher shortage Marathon County schools keep reporting.
access: Proposed rule · submitted to Legislature, no comment deadline listed

name: CR 26-049: DPI rule on Tier I special education licensure dates and who can request them
what: Department of Public Instruction proposes changing effective dates for Tier I special education licenses and which entities may request them; comment open through Oct. 22.
pitch: Tier I licenses are how districts fill special education vacancies with not-yet-fully-licensed staff. Changes shape how Wausau-area districts staff hard-to-fill special ed classrooms.

name: CR 26-050: DPI rule on special education program aide licenses
what: Department of Public Instruction proposes rules on special education program aide licenses, filed with an emergency rule hearing; public comment open through Oct. 22.
pitch: Program aides are the backbone of special education services in local schools. Licensing changes affect hiring, costs, and classroom coverage in Marathon County districts.
access: Proposed rule (emergency rule hearing) · comments through Oct. 22, 2026

name: CR 26-056: DPI would rescind the one-year educational interpreter license
what: Department of Public Instruction proposes rescinding the one-year educational interpreter license; rule filed with hearing information, public comment open through Oct. 22.
pitch: Educational interpreters serve deaf and hard-of-hearing students. Dropping a short-term license pathway could tighten an already thin pipeline for central Wisconsin districts.
